title: POC Milestones and Benchmark Metrics - kickoff & timeline
summary: Kickoff to align on POC milestones: access/setup, workload sizing, benchmark plan, mid-point review, and executive readout. Agreed success criteria (latency, throughput, accuracy/regression limits), a 4-week timeline, and owners for access tasks and benchmark runs.
topics: Workload sizing: concurrency, sequence length, dataset size
Benchmark plan: baseline, Redwood hosted vs dedicated, quantized model variants
Mid-point review and exec readout content
next_steps: Redwood to send POC SOW draft and proposed milestone calendar by 2025-05-09
Customer to share sample dataset and representative prompt set (anonymized) by 2025-05-12
SE to provision logins and test endpoint for baseline runs (hosted) by 2025-05-10
Schedule mid-point review for week of 2025-05-26
Redwood to prepare exec slide template and benchmarking rubric for 2025-05-16
action_items: Lena Park - Draft POC SOW with milestone dates and send - due 2025-05-09
Miguel Santos - Provision hosted test endpoints and sample API key - due 2025-05-10
Sara Kim - Share 10k anonymized prompt/response pairs and throughput target - due 2025-05-12
Priya Rao - Provide firewall/VPC peering requirements and SAML metadata - due 2025-05-11
Tom Ellis - Confirm exec readout attendees and success metrics for execs - due 2025-05-14
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-05-07 15:30 PDT | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Raj (CTO), Sara (ML Eng), Tom (PM), Priya (Sec)

00:00 Lena: Okay, thanks everyone for hopping on. This is Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on this POC. Quick round robin?
00:08 Raj: Raj here, CTO at Aperture Health. We own ingestion and the ML infra. We're looking to validate latency and cost before committing to Dedicated.
00:15 Miguel: Hi all, Miguel SE. I'll run the benchmark scripts and help with quantization/throughput tuning.
00:22 Tom: Tom, PM on the recommendations team. I'll be running acceptance tests from product side.
00:30 Lena: Cool. Agenda — align on milestones: kickoff + access, baseline benchmark hosted, mid-point review, dedicated validation (if needed), exec readout. Also agree success criteria. Any additions?
00:45 Sara: Just to add, we need a clear pass/fail for regression on hallucination rates for our clinical summarization prompts.
00:52 Priya: And security gating: SOC2 controls, KMS integration, and SAML/SSO for access. We'll need an audit log snapshot.
01:05 Lena: Got it. For the timeline we're proposing 4 weeks: week 0 access/setup, week 1 baseline hosted runs, week 2 tuning and dedicated smoke, week 3 mid-point and prep for exec readout. Does that map?
01:17 Raj: That seems OK. Our critical path likely is dataset sanitization and networking for VPC peering.
01:24 Miguel: Right, and we can start with hosted benchmarks to get a baseline numbers quickly while networking progresses.

05:00 Miguel: Quick note about the benchmark harness — we'll run three modes: 1) hosted Redwood with standard FP16, 2) hosted quantized (4-bit where applicable), 3) dedicated instance with reserved capacity. We'll capture p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
05:22 Tom: For concurrency, our real traffic profile is 95% single-user short queries, but under spike tests we need to support 80 concurrent sessions with 512 token windows.
05:33 Sara: Sequence lengths average 120 tokens for summaries, max ~1024 for longer context pulls. We'll provide distributions.
05:40 Miguel: Perfect. For throughput targets, what does Aperture consider acceptable?
05:45 Raj: We want 95th latency under 250ms for the 120-token workflows in production, and tail under 500ms for 512 windows, assuming dedicated. Hosted baseline can be higher but we'd like to understand cost tradeoffs.
06:00 Lena: Noted. We'll include latency targets and cost budget in the rubric. Also define accuracy thresholds: for hallucination/regression, agreed bound of <3% increase in critical errors vs your current baseline.

08:10 Sara: On the evaluation data — we'll anonymize PHI and provide a 10k sample set plus a smaller 500-case golden set for regression detection. Is that size sufficient for you?
08:22 Miguel: Yes, that should be fine. The golden set is key for automated regression checks per push. We'll run an eval suite and produce confusion/FP/FN rates.

10:00 Priya: Security checklist — SAML for SSO, optional VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink, KMS for envelope encryption, and audit logs kept for 90 days. We also need to know where logs are stored and redaction options.
10:18 Lena: We'll share the security pack with SOC2 and our KMS integration notes. For logs we can provide masked logs and a limited retention sandbox for the POC.
10:26 Priya: Also: can Dedicated run in our VPC? We may need an on-prem agent if required.
10:32 Miguel: Dedicated can be deployed in a VPC or private deployment; we have a Private option but that adds several weeks of provisioning. For the POC we recommend starting hosted + VPC peering for the dedicated smoke tests.

13:00 Miguel: On the tooling side, we'll give you a lightweight benchmark harness (python script + docker image). It will produce metrics in CSV and a dashboard export so you can compare model variants.
13:12 Tom: Will the harness simulate your auto-batching behavior? We need realistic latency numbers.
13:18 Miguel: Yes, the harness hits the same API path the runtime uses and preserves batch sizes. We'll run with producer rates that match your concurrency distribution.

15:30 Miguel: Baseline metrics we'll capture: p50, p95, p99 latencies; throughput (tokens/sec); cost per 1M tokens; and regression score on golden set. We'll also track KV cache hit rates for repeated prompts.
15:45 Sara: How do you measure KV cache effectiveness?
15:50 Miguel: We'll seed repeated prefixes from the dataset to see delta; if you have many repeated contexts, caching can drop token compute by up to 30-40% in our internal tests.

18:00 Raj: Some commercial considerations — we may evaluate Redwood versus a GPU-based in-house optimized runtime. Cost delta needs to be clear for 6-12 month horizon. Can you include a mid-term projection?
18:15 Lena: Yes, we'll include modeled unit economics for 6 and 12 month usage tiers. We'll show hosted vs dedicated break-even based on your concurrency assumptions.

21:00 Miguel: About the models — we'll test your primary open model of choice and a quantized variant. If you want we can also run a smaller architecture to evaluate latency. Are you open to trying 4-bit quantization?
21:12 Sara: We are, as long as accuracy remains within the accepted regression thresholds. We'll rely on the golden set to validate.

24:00 Tom: Mid-point review — what should be presented? We expect: baseline numbers, tuning notes, blockers (e.g., networking), and recommended go/no-go call for proceeding to dedicated.
24:12 Lena: Exactly. Mid-point should have a short exec-friendly one-pager plus a more detailed runbook. The final exec readout will be a 15-min deck covering ROI, risks, and recommended config.

26:30 Miguel: On canaries and rollouts — our runtime supports canary percentages and auto-fallback to a lower-cost variant if SLOs are breached. We'll demo that in the tuning week.
26:45 Raj: Good. Also need to capture audit events for each fallback decision. That ties back to Priya's audit requirements.

29:00 Sara: Any constraints on data residency for test logs? We prefer EU storage for anything with EU-sourced data.
29:08 Lena: We'll note the region selection; hosted runs can be pinned to region with our platform. For POC we'll default to us-west but can shift to eu-west by request.

31:00 Miguel: Preliminary schedule suggestion: Kickoff today, access provisioning by Friday 2025-05-09, baseline runs completed by 2025-05-16, tuning/dedicated smoke 2025-05-19 to 2025-05-23, mid-point 2025-05-27, exec readout 2025-06-02. Thoughts?
31:18 Raj: Dates look OK but we need the dataset sanitized by 5/12 to hit baseline by 5/16.
31:26 Lena: We'll set task owners in the SOW.

34:00 Priya: Quick Q: does Redwood store raw prompts in logs by default? We need redaction for PII/PHI.
34:08 Miguel: By default we log masked prompts; you can opt-in for full logs if you want, but for the POC we recommend masked logs and a private s3 bucket for sanitized exports.
34:22 Priya: OK please document that in the security pack.

36:30 Tom: On success criteria — to recap: p95 latency target for 120-token flows <250ms on dedicated, regression on golden set <3% critical errors, throughput scaled to 80 concurrent sessions with acceptable tail latency, and cost per 1M tokens within the agreed budget. Is that everyone?
36:48 Lena: Yes. We'll formalize that in the rubric and SOW.

39:00 Raj: For the exec readout, I want a short ROI slide: cost delta, expected latency improvement, and any blockers. Keep it concise for our COO.
39:12 Lena: We'll prepare a 3-slide executive summary and a detailed appendix.

42:00 Miguel: Any final tech blockers we should know now?
42:06 Sara: Nothing else; main risk is our change freeze window 5/20-5/22 which might delay dedicated provisioning.
42:15 Miguel: We'll plan dedicated smoke before that window.

44:00 Lena: Great. Recap of next steps in chat — I'll follow up with SOW, Miguel will provision hosted endpoints, Priya share SAML metadata, Sara share data sample. We'll target mid-point week of 5/26.
44:18 Raj: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
44:25 Lena: Thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.
